## Design

### 2026-10-17 – # cardboard PoC~

**4h**

# cardboard PoC~

hello! for week 2, i'm making an iris diaphragm mechanism, similar to what you would see in a camera aperture.

i started off by researching and analyzing different style mechanisms based off pre-existing examples. i found a patent for a light control mechanism that i found interesting. it used the straight slots varient on the base piece, so i decided to use that for my proof of concept.

i sketched out the blades style and outline using my sketchbook first, then cut them out and found the idea worked well.

however, one issue i ran into was that i noticed even with the blades being cut from the relatively thin sketchbook paper, they were overlapping too much.

so i thought, if i were to print it, this definately would be much too bulky, and in the end, i had finalized a version where the blade was two sections, and a hinge-like  mechanism pulled the blade back and forth to open and close the iris.

in my poc, the blades are long pieces, which at the time i found intuitive. however, as mentioned in the previous bit, that would cause the mechanism to be too bulky and not feasible for printing, which is why i designed the blades to be shorter.

tldr; made a cardboard/paper proof-of-concept and validated the original premise of my idea while deciding to modify the blade style.

### 2026-10-18 – # FreeCAD-ing

**8h**

# FreeCAD-ing

## v1
i learned how to use basic freeCAD :3

i decided not to stick with openSCAD (which i'd wanted to learn before) and instead just use a graphical cad software, since the learning curve was less severe.

i started by following a youtube tutorial on a guy who'd used a similar straight cutoutslide mechanism that i was going to use in my poc (from the last entry). this helped me make the first iteration, which i changed to have 8 blades and an arc slot.

## v2

for v2, i decided to change up the blade style a bit and try out a different design i came up with. i wondered if it would be possible to use gears to control the opening of the iris. with some help from youtube, i learned how gears in freecad worked, and ended up with these:

![iris-8-gear-blade-mechanism](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Enz5eN54l9lqazRN1RmXsVG67e54hcBG/db5b426f7e22368b30dc3c39dfa50c6d9f7c0e25a8bd0991c4b70114c8170ae6.png)

![iris-8-geared-finished](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Enz5eN54l9lqazRN1RmXsVG67e54hcBG/0e137df32bff8f4bfb2c38a19b8e001fadecc262acc200d3f0d2e0eba7b27655.png)

## v3

for v3, i wanted to change the design to something that didn't really exist online yet.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Enz5eN54l9lqazRN1RmXsVG67e54hcBG/f3e046e23577ebb26ee13f4c828bd636bacb93b61cb8f9dd37c78108da07a509.png)

in this version, each blade has a link which is connected to the blade at one point and connected to the ring at another point.

i chose ten to be the number of blades... kind of on a whim, lol. i'd already done 8 and i wanted 12 to be the final version, so 10 in between.

## final version plans

right now, i want to do a arc slot style mechanism for moving the blades, and as mentioned above, i'm planning to implement 12 blades this time.

tl;dr:
- v1: first iteration with 8 blades and common arc slot mechanism
- v2: again 8 blades, this time experimenting with gears
- v3: ten blade linkage variant
- future: 12 blade arc slot style blade opening

# final model

i designed the final model to have 12 blades and a similar arc slot mechanism i used for v1. alternating blades sit on different height pegs attached to the base, which allows this 12-blade model (which would usually be much thicker at 25-35mm) to only be 8.75mm.

## fun side piece

after finishing the above final version, i had inspiration suddenly to make a new opening mechanism using semicircles and arc slots to fit the pegs.

the result wasn't as slim/short as the final, but the circle formed by the blades overlapping was much smoother. i'm not sure how the smoothness of the turning would translate to real life, though.
